confirming.Constraints and boundaries: Use public aggregated data only for all data. Focus on first principles, use tried-and-true engines, and do not reinvent the wheel. The simulation should approximate real healthcare effects where defensible without claiming clinical validation; assumptions and uncertainty must remain visible.

AGENTS.md establishes staged SDLC workflows (observed 2026-10-23; re-check if workflow instructions change). Stage 01 preserves unresolved consequential discovery decisions. confirming.Open questions and deferrals: No operator-only decision blocks this draft. Engine selection, executable path, data sources, calibration, and validation method remain implementation and discovery work rather than settled operator choices. The healthcare-simulation validation standard remains unknown and should be assigned to the planning/design owner.
confirming.Owners and next steps: The implementation team should identify a proven engine, establish the simulation and data boundaries, document public aggregated sources and transformations, and define behavior-specific tests. The planning/design owner should determine the validation approach and guard against presenting assumptions as clinical facts. The operator remains the decider for any later consequential scope or product trade-off.
confirming.Problem statement: The repository currently describes the intended healthcare tycoon concept but contains no established gameplay implementation or test modules. The first change therefore needs to establish a playable simulation architecture rather than modify existing gameplay. The problem matters because the game must make clinic, budget, capacity, and patient-outcome decisions visibly and credibly interact.
confirming.Proposed outcome: A bounded playable browser management loop for several clinics: allocate constrained budget and capacity, advance time, serve a population grounded in documented public aggregated data, and observe explainable differences in access, queues, costs, and outcome indicators. The first version should use a proven engine, keep flows and bottlenecks visible, and clearly distinguish observed data from simulation assumptions.
confirming.Risks and verification: Key risks are invented or private data, unsupported clinical claims, opaque causal relationships, and architecture that expands beyond a testable first loop. Mitigate with source and transformation records, explicit assumptions and uncertainty, deterministic simulation tests, engine build/type checks, and browser interaction checks. Proposed checks are listed below; none have been run. Where we did not look: implementation source, test suites, CI configuration, engine configuration, and external public-data documentation.
